chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Nu'ayn ibn Shu'ayb al-Naysaburi, from Yasin al-Darir, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) who said:
"Do not fast on the day of Ashura, nor on the day of Arafah in Mecca, nor in Medina, nor in your homeland, nor in any of the provinces."

key_terms.عَاشُورَاءَ: The 10th of Muharram, a significant day in the Islamic calendar.
key_terms.وَطَنِكَ: Your homeland or place of residence.
key_terms.يَوْمَ عَرَفَةَ: The Day of Arafah, the 9th of Dhu al-Hijjah.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on Ashura and Arafah in one's hometown?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a specific legal nuance regarding the fasting of Ashura and Arafah, prohibiting it when performed in one's hometown or major cities (amsar), likely to distinguish these days from the general practice of voluntary fasting or to emphasize their unique status. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on contextualizing religious observances based on location, ensuring that the distinct spiritual significance of these days is preserved rather than conflated with routine devotional acts.
